title: Sub-Bottom Profiler Vertical Resolution

V_s.description: Acoustic velocity in sediment (1500–1800 m/s typical)

applicability: Higher frequency = better resolution but less penetration. Chirp (2–16 kHz): 0.05–0.5 m resolution, 10–50 m penetration. Boomer (0.5–5 kHz): 0.5–1 m resolution, 50–100 m penetration. Sparker (0.1–1 kHz): 1–2 m resolution, 100+ m penetration.

title: Side-Scan Sonar Range and Resolution
equation: Swath width = 2 × Range;  Along-track resolution ≈ R × λ / L
applicability: 100 kHz: 300–600 m range, ~1 m resolution. 400 kHz: 75–150 m range, ~0.2 m resolution. Tow altitude typically 10–20% of range setting. Speed typically 3–5 knots for survey quality.

title: Multibeam Echo Sounder Depth Accuracy
applicability: IHO S-44 Order 1a: THU = 2m + 1% depth, TVU = √(0.25² + (0.0075×d)²). Outer beams have lower accuracy than nadir. RTK-GPS positioning eliminates tide uncertainty.

title: Vibrocore Penetration — Empirical
equation: L_core ≈ L_barrel × (0.6 to 0.9)  depending on soil type

L_barrel.description: Core barrel length (typically 3–6 m, max ~12 m)

applicability: Vibrocore effective in soft sediments (clay, silt, loose sand). Recovery ratio typically 60–90% in soft soils, decreasing in dense sand/gravel. Core shortening (compression) common in soft clays. Maximum practical depth ~12 m below seabed.

title: Wave-Induced Vessel Heave — Significant Height
applicability: Drilling operability limited by vessel motion. Typical limits: jack-up barge: unlimited (fixed). DP vessel: Hs < 2.0–3.0 m for CPT/drilling. Anchored barge: Hs < 1.0–1.5 m. Heave compensation required for deepwater sampling.

title: Seabed CPT Correction for Water Depth
equation: σ_v0 = γ_sub × z_seabed  (effective stress below mudline only)

σ_v0.description: Effective vertical stress for CPT interpretation

γ_sub.description: Submerged unit weight of seabed soil

z_seabed.description: Depth below mudline (not below water surface)

applicability: Water column pressure acts equally on cone and soil — does not affect qt, fs, or u2 interpretation. All CPT correlations use depth below mudline. Pore pressure sensor: u2 offset must account for hydrostatic water column pressure (calibrated before deployment).

title: Grab Sampler Penetration (Van Veen / Smith-McIntyre)
applicability: Grab samplers collect disturbed surficial material for classification, contamination assessment, and benthic studies. Not suitable for geotechnical strength parameters. Volume typically 5–30 L depending on grab size and soil type.

title: Acoustic Impedance Contrast (Reflection Coefficient)
equation: R = (Z₂ - Z₁) / (Z₂ + Z₁)  where Z = ρ × V
applicability: Governs strength of reflections in sub-bottom profiler data. Strong contrasts (soft clay over rock: R ≈ 0.5–0.8) produce bright reflectors. Weak contrasts (clay over silt: R ≈ 0.05–0.10) may not be resolved. Water-seabed interface typically R ≈ 0.1–0.4.
